A verdict whose detail simply OMITS event_id/status/terminal_verified/scheduled_start_utc turns the entire cluster-E guard off. The 8/30 BOS@NYY fabrication is then written to sink=result_ledger with settleable=True and served by every analysis tool.
STILL_OPEN_HIGH.evidence:
harness/verified_snapshot.py:676-717 (_verdict_binding_problems), re-used verbatim at :1167 (_assert_servable) so the read-path re-check has the same hole. RUN (verbatim output):
  admit() says: REJECT_PRESTART_OR_UNBOUND
  sink_for(forged) = result_ledger  settleable = True
  WROTE: vsnap1_6dc9b8e3...
  get_verified_score SERVED: {"away_score":0,"home_score":1,"event_id":"mlb:2026:SYNTHETIC-UNVERIFIED-BOSNYY-0830","source":"web_search","source_fetched_at_utc":"2026-08-30T17:30:00Z","status":"CLOSED"}

The record is the incident record: source "web_search", observed 5 minutes BEFORE first pitch (17:35Z), which sa.admit() correctly returns REJECT_PRESTART_OR_UNBOUND for. The verdict handed to write_snapshot was four keys: {disposition: ADMIT_FINAL, reason_codes: [STATUS_VALIDATED], admissible_as: FINAL, detail: {lane: CANONICAL}}. Nothing was forged that had to match anything — the guard is switched off by DELETING keys, not by faking them. The docstring discloses a different, HARDER residual ("a record re-fabricated to match the verdict ... still passes") and does not disclose this one. test_verdict_copied_from_another_record only exercises the COPY shape, so the fixture cannot see the omission shape.

STILL_OPEN_HIGH.claim: REGRESSION of cluster D. The read path's payload re-hash is memoized on (relative path, st_size, st_mtime_ns). An archive that rewrites payload bytes under an unchanged filename while preserving size and mtime — the exact mutable-archive threat this module names — is served by all three analysis tools after the snapshot has been read once in the process, while verify_snapshot() on the same bytes reports RAW_PAYLOAD_BYTES_DRIFTED.
STILL_OPEN_HIGH.evidence:
harness/verified_snapshot.py:1105-1114 (_cached_payload_drift) and :1068-1082 (_fs_signature: path, st_size, st_mtime_ns only). RUN (verbatim):
  read1 served: True
  same size: True  same mtime_ns: True  bytes changed: True
  READ2 SERVED — cache hid the payload drift: mlb:2026:...MIAWSH-0830 2 9
  verify_snapshot ok: False ['RAW_PAYLOAD_BYTES_DRIFTED','SNAPSHOT_ID_NO_LONGER_MATCHES_CONTENT','RECORD_HASH_NO_LONGER_COVERED_BY_A_PAYLOAD']
  READ3 (cache cleared) refused: SnapshotImmutabilityViolation
The getter and verify_snapshot disagree about the same directory in the same process, which is precisely the split cluster D was raised about. Note DRIFT_ID_NOT_CONTENT does not save it: the content digest covers the payload DESCRIPTORS (declared sha), not the bytes on disk, so the cached payload re-hash is the only thing between an edited raw payload and get_verified_score. Every existing drift fixture writes new bytes without restoring mtime, so no fixture ever exercises a warm cache.

STILL_OPEN_HIGH.suggested_fix: Either drop _cached_payload_drift from the read path entirely (verify_snapshot is already uncached and _read_integrity re-hashes the entry files on every call, so the payload half is the only cached one), or make the cache key unforgeable by an archive rewrite: include st_ino, st_ctime_ns and st_dev, and invalidate the whole entry whenever _read_integrity finds any drift. MUTANT to add: write a snapshot, read it once to warm the cache, rewrite a payload byte preserving size and mtime with os.utime, and require the second get_verified_score to raise SnapshotImmutabilityViolation on a NAMED assertion.
